newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian top 7 forex reserves match G7 - Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Asian top 7 forex reserves match G7 - Singapore.

text.p: The foreign exchange reserves of the top seven Asian countries are equal to those of the Group of Seven industrialised nations, Singapore's Finance Minister Richard Hu told a conference on Friday.
"The aggregate reserves of the top seven Asian countries matches that of the G7 countries," Hu told the annual conference of the International Securities Market Association (ISMA).
Hu's comments follow the recent speculative attack against the Thai baht in which the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) -- of which Hu is chairman -- intervened to help defend the currency.
Many Asian central banks have repurchase pacts between each other which enable them to defend another country's currency using that country's holdings of U.S. Treasury securities as collateral.
Hu noted Singapore is the fourth most active foreign exchange trading centre in the world. "Daily turnover in Singapore's foreign exchange market averaged US$130 billion in 1996."
"Of this, only about six percent actually involved trading in the Singapore dollar," he added.
Turning to the prospects for Asia, Hu said the ongoing economic liberalisation in China, India and Indo-China is expected to unleash the next wave of economic growth in Asia.

"A recent World Bank study indicated that the Asian economies will expand at an average rate of 7.2 percent annually over the next 10 years, which is almost three times that of the industrialised countries," he said.
Hu said Asia's full growth potential can be realised only if there is efficient access to capital.

"Large infrastructure investments will cause demand for funds to exceed domestic savings in many countries. This will compel the Asian economies to look within and beyond the region for surplus capital," Hu said.
He said that over the next decade Asian financial markets will have to modify their traditional role of channelling funds from the developed economies.

"The key challenge for Asia in the next decade is therefore to sustain the healthy development of its financial markets, which is critical to fostering continued macro-economic growth of the region," he said. -- Singapore newsroom 65-8703080
